facts.fact: 叙述者承认「Ida 显灵」也许是一种可能，但想不出她为什么要费心毁一本旧速写本；她断定凶手是活人——能进她房间的三个人里，只有一个在 Uncle Leon 的日记里出现过恶形恶状。
facts.anchor: The culprit had to be a real person, and only one of the three people with access to my room had featured negatively in Uncle Leon’s journal

facts.fact: 周六下午，叙述者待在阳光房里观察院子，发现草一夜之间朝房子推进了三英尺；她自问这是不是 Ironheart 在悄悄扩张地盘。
facts.anchor: which had grown three feet closer to the house overnight. If I hadn’t seen the border before, I may not have known it ever existed

facts.fact: 车里，叙述者直接问 Leon 是否留下过速写本；Gazzie 握着方向盘指节发白，答「Probably. Ginny would know where they are」，随即把收音机音量拧大、终结谈话——她承认速写本可能存在，却讳于多谈。
facts.anchor: Turning up the radio, Gazzie signaled the end of our chat. She’d admitted to the sketchbooks’ potential existence but seemed reluctant to discuss them.

facts.fact: 在派对上，叙述者说岛上人对 Gazzie 的出现一律有反应；她回述 Ida Greer 早在杀死那条传奇鳄鱼时就已在镇上恶名在外，而她——一个女人、从前当过女仆——后来索性干起猎鳄生意、建了养殖场，更添话柄。
facts.anchor: Ida Greer had been infamous in the town as soon as she’d killed the legendary alligator, even more so when she—a woman! a former lady’s maid!—started an alligator hunting business, then the farm.

facts.fact: Aunt Virginia 把手搭在 Henri 腹上，向叙述者介绍她时称她「Dart」；此前她看到 Gazzie 时笑容塌了一分又扳回原位。
facts.anchor: Placing her hand on the tall woman’s stomach, she said, “Dart, this is Henri.”

facts.fact: 叙述者看着 Aunt Virginia 与 Henri，对速写本的焦虑被冲走；她说从没见过两个人爱得这么明显，并承认「属于一个人」的感觉想必美好。
facts.anchor: I’d never known two people so obviously in love. It must feel wonderful to belong to someone like that. To have someone belong to you.

facts.fact: 叙述者复述 Gazzie 场外喊出的要领「Legs apart. Axe up. Eye on the center of the wood」后挥斧，原木齐整裂成两半；胸口的紧绷随木头倒下松开，她咧嘴笑了，Gazzie 的笑容「took ten years off her」。
facts.anchor: It split squarely in two, both halves tumbling over their respective sides. As they fell, the tightness in my chest loosened, and I grinned.

facts.fact: 火堆边 Harrison 说想到她就看见「握刀、围裙浸血」的人、说他知道她藏了很多；他的目光落到她唇上，这一次没有立刻收回；他倾身半寸时 Aunt Virginia 在身后喝止「Cut it out」，章末 Harrison「looked stunned」。
facts.anchor: Firelight sparkled in Harrison’s eyes. They were the dark blue of the night sky as they dropped to my lips. This time, they didn’t immediately return to my face.
